source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #348 (branch fix/342-handle-transfer at head 01bbf1e3fdb04413d08214ef421921305714c39b — the #342 change (canonical lift/lower transfers resource handles across component call boundaries: own handles move between the per-instance handle tables introduced by #317, and borrows register in the destination table for the duration of the call) merged with current main 90f1437b1445b8523daa2f78eecb366de415ed11 (PRs #340, #345 and #346), with the single exclusion-table conflict in component_model_upstream.rs resolved by dropping both the #333 clause (fixed by #346) and the #317 clause (superseded by #317 and this PR) from linking/unit.wast's exclusion reason, and one test assertion updated to the trap cause #312's preservation now surfaces; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45574460897, 45574476400 and 45574496024 against the branch and pull-request run 45573469477, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #348 (#342, canonical lift/lower transfers resource handles across component call boundaries). The branch merged current main (merge commit 634bfd3, main at 90f1437b1445b8523daa2f78eecb366de415ed11 — PRs #340 (#312, trap on unaligned canonical ABI pointers), #345 (#332, realloc called when lowering empty lists) and #346 (#333, defined instances materialised in definition order) on top of the #341/#343 base the branch started from) and its CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate on the 12 series of the three configurations that link telomere-component. The merge conflicted only in the vendored-suite exclusion table (component_model_upstream.rs, the linking/unit.wast reason): main had dropped the #333 clause (fixed by #346) while this branch dropped the #317 clause (superseded by #317 and this PR); the resolution drops both clauses, leaving #321 (line 799), #324 (lines 2010, 2043) and the alias export-resolution failure at lines 865-866, filed as #347. One test assertion was updated for the trap cause #312's preservation now surfaces — the wrong-type drop test in component_resource_handles.rs pins the ‘resource handle 2 is invalid’ message; the test still requires the trap. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45574513443, 45574531337 and 45574550157 on main at 90f1437b1445b8523daa2f78eecb366de415ed11; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline). Against the checked-in baseline, the main control is byte-identical on 20 of the 32 gated series; on the 12 series of the three configurations that link telomere-component it measures uniformly below that baseline — stripped file and stripped .text −96 B in release and −32 B in release-size, in each of component, wasi and wasi-threads — because that baseline was snapshotted from PR #340's branch tree and the squash-merged main measures slightly smaller (the gate passes shrinkage, so the staleness was inert). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the same 12 series: in release, stripped file +6,744 B (component), +6,744 B (wasi) and +6,728 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +5,552 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +4,648 B / +4,648 B / +4,664 B and stripped .text +3,664 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +10.29% (2,433,656 B to 2,683,928 B), up from +10.01%; the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
